answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral before joining, so a Sybil attacker pays the bond for every clone. Like a dune that shifts yet holds its shape, the network keeps honest weight stable while clones wash away. A steady pulse of work, periodic proofs of useful computation, keeps idle copies from harvesting rewards, and a harbor of verified reputation lets peers dock trust only with agents that delivered consistently, raising the cost of starting over under a new name.
